title: European Nicotinamide Diabetes Intervention Trial (ENDIT): a randomised controlled trial of intervention before the onset of type 1 diabetes
design: Double-blind randomized trial. 552 relatives with islet-cell antibodies and a glucose tolerance test below the diabetes threshold received nicotinamide (vitamin B3) or placebo.
endpoint: Clinical diabetes by WHO criteria during five years of planned treatment.
result: Diabetes developed in 82 nicotinamide recipients and 77 placebo recipients. Adjusted hazard ratio 1.01 (95% CI 0.73–1.38). Serious adverse event counts were similar.
limit: 168 of 552 participants withdrew. The interval permits a smaller benefit or harm. The study did not test treatment after diagnosis.

title: Ergocalciferol in New-onset Type 1 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial
design: Single-center, double-blind vitamin D2 versus placebo trial. Each arm had 18 young people aged 10–21 with residual insulin secretion.
endpoint: Stimulated C-peptide concentration over 12 months; HbA1c and daily insulin dose were also measured.
result: The original report found no statistically significant between-group difference in stimulated C-peptide concentration at individual visits (reported P=0.08) or daily insulin dose. HbA1c rose more slowly on vitamin D2 in a trend analysis.
limit: Small cohort with measurable insulin production at enrollment. Persistence after treatment ended is unknown. The 2024 secondary report analyzes these same participants.
locator: PubMed abstract, Methods and Results. The original analysis reports concentrations at visits.
access: Public abstract checked; full text available (PMC8668202).

title: Effect of Ergocalciferol on β-Cell Function in New-Onset Type 1 Diabetes: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial
design: Secondary analysis of the same 36 randomized participants in the 12-month vitamin D2 trial (PMID 34913020).
endpoint: Monthly trend in percent change from baseline in meal-stimulated C-peptide area under the curve, integrating measurements across the meal test.
result: The estimated monthly change was −2.8% (SE 0.7%) with vitamin D2 versus −4.7% (SE 0.6%) with placebo; P=0.03 for the trend comparison.
limit: This uses another measurement and model in the original cohort. It adds no independent replication or post-treatment follow-up and does not establish a durable benefit.
locator: JAMA Network Open, Methods and Results; Figure, panel C.

title: No Protective Effect of Calcitriol on β-Cell Function in Recent-Onset Type 1 Diabetes: The IMDIAB XIII Trial
design: Independent, double-blind randomized trial. 34 people aged 11–35 received calcitriol (active vitamin D) or placebo for two years.
endpoint: Basal C-peptide over two years; meal-stimulated C-peptide response at 12 months.
result: C-peptide fell by 44.4% with calcitriol and 42.5% with placebo by 24 months. Groups showed no significant differences in C-peptide, HbA1c or insulin requirements at the reported visits.
limit: 27 of 34 completed follow-up. The sample size calculation targeted a 0.12 nmol/L basal C-peptide difference at two years. The formulation and endpoints differ from the vitamin D2 trial.
locator: Diabetes Care 33:1962–1963, Statistical power and analysis, Results, and Conclusions.
access: Public full text checked against the university-hosted article.

title: Effects of dietary supplementation in treatment and control of progression and complications of insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus: a systematic review with meta-analyses of randomized clinical trials
design: Systematic review and meta-analyses of randomized trials. Outcomes and vitamin D formulations varied between trials.
endpoint: Fasting C-peptide pooled across four reports (144 participants); HbA1c pooled separately.
result: The pooled fasting C-peptide result favored vitamin D (P=0.023), but the authors rated the evidence very low quality. The pooled HbA1c result did not show a significant benefit.
limit: This is a synthesis, not a newly enrolled cohort. Its fasting C-peptide analysis includes the original Nwosu trial (reference 36). A shared off-treatment follow-up period was not established.
locator: Results, Effects of vitamin D supplementation, Figures 2B and 3B; reference 36 identifies Nwosu.
access: Public full text checked in SciELO.
